column1: # The routes and what must hold on each replay: tools/check_routes.py (ctest oracles-routes, with ORACLES_ROM_DIR set).

# Link's sprite as drawn goes back on the screen three times in overworld.route (enhanced.link_backsteps_y): the camera's catch-up stepping on a frame his sprite does not, and twice his jump off a ledge, his height drawn while the camera follows the ground; and once across (enhanced.link_backsteps), at 3722, the scroll down from 0:c6 into 0:d6 loading: the frames of the load show the sprite the game drew before it, a pixel short of his place the camera catches up on.

# With the settling camera Link's sprite never goes back across (enhanced.link_backsteps, once with the previous camera), and the band shows 45 objects fading out at the rooms left (enhanced.faded_out_objects), one fewer, leaving their place sooner.
# overworld.route in the far view fitted to the screen (--screen): 426x320 on 1280x960, 412x360 on 1240x1080, the rules of its far 4:3 rows.
# overworld.route in the view's other sizes (docs/REFERENCE.md): near in 4:3, medium in 16:9 and 4:3.

# overworld.route in the far view with the status bar full width: the houses' loads keep the band as in play; the play area moves once, at the end of the first load, where Link walks out of his house into a room the camera only frames once he is in it.

# On mGBA, continuous-transitions.route parts from its recording: at frame 6611 the game's logic on mGBA does not read the keys for three frames, still busy, where SameBoy reads them at once, so that A is held three frames less; it parts after 29 rooms in common. The row below holds mGBA's replay of it.

# Enhanced on mGBA, continuous-transitions.route: it parts on mGBA from its recording, as the comment on its faithful rows says. Replayed to frame 6600, just before, it shows on mGBA SameBoy's figures (one vertical camera jump, no jump of Link, 79 frames waiting for a neighbour): the jumps above the row of SameBoy's are mGBA's game's, after the parting.
# continuous-transitions.route with the status bar drawn full width: the white fades, a dungeon's large rooms, and on SameBoy Subrosia's colours (mGBA's replay parts before, as above).

# neighbour-objects.route with the objects' animation stepped from the game's data against the live game (--object-animation-check), Horon's villagers, fountain and flowers: a neighbour animates an object by the rule, its code advancing its animation by one call of the step at each update of the capture's probe, and the probe's verdict is the game's on its first updates after each scroll (41 objects); of the animated, the game's changes by its data are all the step's and the step's are the game's, none wrong while Link is away; kept still by the rule, seven captured objects of several poses, among them the springbloom flowers of 0:c6 ($9c, still in their state 1 until Link touches them) and, judged on the game where no capture pairs them, Vasu's snakes ($89, set back to their animation's start each update until Link comes near), whose 178 changes by the step the game does not make (not_animated); every pose shown live has its tiles in the capture; the fountain's spurt of 0:e7 ($4c:07) is an entry or two ahead of its capture after the scroll, its code restarting its loop as Link arrives (entry_different, three captures).
# With the settling camera the band, placed elsewhere, shows a neighbour's people for a frame less: 825 pose changes drawn (enhanced.pose_changes_drawn), the previous camera 826.

# neighbour-objects.route in the far view, Horon's villagers, flowers and fountain animated in place in the rooms around: the cost of the poses' renders, under the frame's budget of the tiles' animation.

# With the settling camera the band, placed elsewhere, shows the neighbours' people for fewer frames: 1755 pose changes drawn (enhanced.pose_changes_drawn), the previous camera 1769. With the ghosts' new order the camera, holding toward the rooms being prepared, places the band elsewhere again: 1751.
# lost-woods.route in the far view fitted to the screen (--screen): 426x320 on 1280x960, 412x360 on 1240x1080, the rules of its far 4:3 rows.

# hotkeys-throw.route with the item hotkeys' live policy in `use` and scripted keys: the bombs' key lifts a bomb at 1300 and throws it at 1345, as B does; the power bracelet's key picks it up at 1368 and throws it at 1398; the bombs' key lifts another at 1550 and the feather's key throws it at 1590, nothing exchanged, no jump; the three throws are presses of their own, not uses.  Before, the second press was dropped (hotkeys.live.throws=0).
# hotkeys-throw.route in `equip`: the bombs on B, the bracelet on A, and the bombs' key again gives B its sword back, each with the inventory's equip sound.
# intro.route: the night Onox's arrival puts on the troupe's camp (cutscene06Func4, from 5280 to 7032), which the neighbouring rooms take with the game's window.

# With the ghosts running the corners a scroll would bring into the band, two more terrains computed ahead are dropped when a byte of the key they read changes in the intro: 34 (enhanced.drops), 32 before.

# intro.route: a room run again for its objects whose run comes back while the live game is held (a text box, a menu, a scene) is put off, not failed (enhanced.objects_refresh_put_off), and no room loses its objects (enhanced.objects_story_dropped); the room a scroll left is drawn from its image, never from its entry kept out of date (enhanced.left_stale_frames: 0:a7's for 33 frames when it was kept).

# intro.route: where a scene ends in a fade, the game puts Link back as the picture comes back; brought to rest behind the fade, the camera stands where it stays from the first frame seen, Link still (enhanced.return_glide_frames, enhanced.return_glide_pixels: 4 frames and 7 px before as it panned and settled over to him, 8 frames and 12 px in 4:3 with the sub-pixel camera). With the sub-pixel camera the run hash moves for the split of that place into whole pixels and a fraction (1121 less 223/256 rather than 1120 and 33/256), the picture the same to a pixel of the screen.

# The ghost in its thread holds it as well, paced or not: the tint takes the room's palettes from its entry, delivered before the scene (dropped by the dance, its palettes kept), and needs no run during it.
# intro.route with the rooms never visited kept dark (--unvisited-rooms hidden): a new game, each room fading in at its first entry; the black under the rows' without it.

# With the settling camera the band, framing Link without the look-ahead where he stops, once shows 12 rooms kept dark at a time (enhanced.hidden_rooms_max), the previous camera 11. With the ghosts running the corners a scroll would bring into the band, two more terrains computed ahead are dropped when a byte of the key they read changes (enhanced.drops 34, 32 before), and the edge fades, an exact count that follows the order the rooms are computed in, are 12 (15 before).
# intro.route with the rooms never visited kept dark in a small console's views: far 4:3 with the sub-pixel camera, and medium 4:3, the RG DS's default.
# With the settling camera two dark rooms' pixels arrive before the band shows them bare: 12 edge fades (enhanced.edge_fades), the previous camera 14.

# dungeon.route: Link's sprite goes back on the screen against the step before twice across (enhanced.link_backsteps), walking at a pixel a frame through the large rooms, where the camera in whole pixels waits a frame and then makes up two pixels on his step.
# dungeon.route in the far view fitted to the screen (--screen): 426x320 on 1280x960, 412x360 on 1240x1080, the rules of its far 4:3 rows.
# dungeon.route in the view's other sizes (docs/REFERENCE.md): near in 4:3, medium in 16:9 and 4:3.
# dungeon.route with the status bar drawn full width, far and near 4:3: the bands of the narrow gutters too.

# On mGBA, swim.route parts from its recording at frame 626: in the load that follows the screen turned back on, the game's logic of frame 626 ends just before the vblank on mGBA, just after it on SameBoy, and every input after is read a frame earlier; the forced swims are not reached. The row below holds mGBA's replay of it.

# swim.route: after a fade, the camera moves only with Link, his fraction of a pixel counted with the sub-pixel camera (enhanced.return_glide_frames: 3 frames counted before on the sub-pixel row, Link setting off by fractions of a pixel).
# Enhanced on mGBA, swim.route: it parts on mGBA from its recording, as the comment on its faithful rows says: the figures of the row below are those of mGBA's game.

# swim.route with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel), each core's game: where the picture switches (a scroll starting or ending, a text box opening or closing, Link drawn apart or no longer) the band's step changes by 4 px of the screen at most (enhanced.switch_band_jolt_max): at a scroll's first frame (3058, 3290) the band stops while it gives its fraction back, the camera still going through the game's hold of Link, then takes the camera's whole pixel; where it dropped its fraction for the scroll before, up to 4 px at once; Link's by 5 at most (7 before he was drawn apart through the scrolls, where the game moves his sprites itself); his layer coming or going in a scroll no longer moves him against the ground by his own fraction, up to 3 px of the screen 61 times before (enhanced.transition_layer_shift_max).
# swim.route in far 4:3, the shape where the corners of the drawn-back band show outside the scrolls: on each core, as above.

# stairs-diagonal.route: Link up and down the stairs of 0:d9, then diagonally in 0:e9, written by hand; his sprite as the frame draws it never goes back on the screen against the step before (enhanced.link_backsteps), in every size of the view and with both camera profiles. Without the sub-pixel camera the band steps with his whole steps, as the game does: its stops between two of them (enhanced.band_stops) are held at 61, the previous camera's 41 moving him on the screen instead.

# stairs-diagonal.route with Link drawn in phase on a diagonal walk (--enhanced-link-phase, a trial, off by default): the stairs are left as they were; in 0:e9's diagonals the camera steps back across the walk twice instead of 12 times (enhanced.camera_wobble), and his sprite never goes back on the screen.

# stairs-diagonal.route with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel): at 4x the band stops between two of its steps 10 times an axis instead of 41, and steps back across the walk once instead of 12 times.

# stairs-diagonal.route with the sub-pixel camera switched off and on again six times during the walk (--enhanced-subpixel-switch), as Display's Camera from the pause: no jolt past the Pixel camera's, Link never left in the band nor drawn twice; the band's stops between its steps half way between the two cameras' (10 and 41), nearly all in the Pixel span from 1320, where the whole camera steps with Link's whole steps on both axes at once and so stops on both.

# swim-hold.route: swim.route's start, Link entering the water with the flippers, then with the swim's hold (its header's option) a direction held alone, with A, then nothing; on SameBoy alone, swim.route parting on mGBA at its frame 626, before any swim.

# diagonal-crossings.route: Link crossing the edges of 0:e7, 0:e8, 0:d7 and 0:d8 diagonally in the eight ways, written by hand; with --continuous-diagonal a diagonal held carries him across the scroll's axis too (transitions.carried_frames), and the frames he stands across it two frames running (enhanced.scroll_across_stalled) are those a wall across holds him, in 0:d7's bottom row, and those whose game frame ends past the vblank, which moves nothing; every key changes between two scrolls. In the scroll from 0:e7 into 0:e8 the game draws its frame of 3355 at line 142 on SameBoy, 141 on mGBA, and its main loop waits for the vblank (wVBlankChecker) on mGBA only: from 3356 SameBoy runs a frame behind, through the same rooms entered on the same frames, its carries and walls a frame apart, which give the same counts on both but in the scroll left from 0:d8 into 0:d7: Link enters it 1.4 px higher on SameBoy (3869) than on mGBA (3871), and the carry the room's load withheld, caught up once its collisions are known, takes him to the wall of 0:d7's bottom row two frames later on SameBoy (transitions.carried_frames 292 there, 290 on mGBA). Its start is continuous-transitions.route's, whose two ghost runs into a wrong room before 0:e7 the drawn-back and sized rows forbid: the normal band only.

# diagonal-crossings.route on foot as the OAM draws him (walk.drawn_off_scroll_frames, as on Ages' line-edges.route): his sprite follows the game's own step at the frames that start a scroll, 27 frames so before on SameBoy, 5 since.

# diagonal-crossings.route with Link drawn in phase on a diagonal walk (--enhanced-link-phase): the camera steps back across the walk 8 times instead of 37 on SameBoy, 13 instead of 50 on mGBA; the game is the same (the transitions' counts), his sprite never goes back on the screen.

# diagonal-crossings.route with the sub-pixel camera (--enhanced-subpixel): at 4x the band stops between two of its steps 17 times an axis instead of 79 (16 on mGBA), and steps back across the walk once instead of 36 times (never instead of 54 on mGBA); the game is the same.
# diagonal-crossings.route with the transitions' steps (--continuous-steps, ages/checks.tsv says what they count): the frame that
# ends a scroll gives Link his step on all 21 scrolls, where without them it left him still on 21 (the same frame, the phase that
# ends the scroll, as in Ages), and no diagonal start doubles his step across, 12 without them.

# With the sub-pixel camera: at 4x the band stops between two of its steps 19 times an axis on 18 frames, 16 on mGBA (17 and 15 without the steps), 9 of those frames where Link himself stands still on that axis, the camera stopping with him. Link's step changes by 14 px at the start and the end of the scroll out of a large room (1354, 1386), the game carrying him at the scroll's speed: drawn at his fraction of a pixel there, his half pixels come and go and those frames count as a switch, where before they counted elsewhere (enhanced.link_jolt_max, 16). In a scroll, Link as shown dips back by 3 px or more at 4x against his step then goes on 6 times, 2 with the steps (enhanced.scroll_link_dips): the game holding him a frame while the band moves on; one of them is now 3 px where it was 5, his sprites drawn at his place where an OAM left uncopied had them a pixel behind.
# swim-steps.route: swim.route's inputs adjusted for the steps on land, with their diagonal, as the home screen plays
# them (its header says where): eight transitions swum at the surface with the flippers, his motion carrying him across the
# scrolls' axis (transitions.carried_frames), through the recording's rooms on both cores, a few frames off its times (its
# header says where).  No scroll's last frame leaves him still, no start doubles his step.

# swim-steps.route: after a fade, the camera moves only with Link, his fraction of a pixel counted with the sub-pixel camera (enhanced.return_glide_frames: 2 frames counted before on the sub-pixel row, Link setting off by fractions of a pixel).
# With the sub-pixel camera: from 1511 the replay swims a path of its own (its header says where), through other places at
# each frame than the replay before it, and the camera follows that path: the band stops 19 times an axis on it (12 on the path
# before), every one on a frame where Link himself stands still on that axis, the camera stopping with him.

# swim-line.route: Link swimming at the surface with the flippers, the transitions at the line. Every frame of normal play the policy's step of his swim is the game's own, strokes and glides (transitions.swim_model_mismatched=0); through each scroll he swims by that step, the machine's own move undone and nothing pushing him, and the three taps at the end, whose strokes and glides cross the edge between 0:74 and 0:75, go exactly as far as they would in the middle of a room (swim.edge_glides_unlike=0). Of the scroll frames, those he goes otherwise than his motion are walls the game holds him at as well, and one frame the game's load ran past its vblank (2931, the scroll's end then counted a stall, transitions.end_stalls=1). Two corners carry him past the line across into the room beside, one turn in a scroll swims him back past the line (transitions.cross_started=3 with the scroll back). On mGBA the replay parts from SameBoy's at the 21st room (3369: SameBoy enters 0:85, mGBA 0:76 at 3521), its walks on land a frame or two apart since 712, and its taps at the end fall elsewhere; its own rows hold the same rules. On mGBA, at 3494, a glide up along 0:75's right edge, his angle 6 steps off it, starts the scroll into 0:76 as soon as his next step crosses the line, where the game once put him back on it to slide along it for 26 frames. On mGBA, a scroll up whose glide would end in the room's last rows under a swimmer's line, where the game would take him out of the water, carries him over it by the scroll's end: one frame lifted (transitions.swim_lifted_frames=1), counted with those he goes otherwise than his motion.

# shop.route: overworld.route's keys to Horon's shop (0:e6), then bombs put on B, one dropped and its blast taken, the shop entered (3:a6) and ten bombs bought for 20 rupees, written by hand.  With --cheats no-damage,rupees the blast costs no heart and the purchase nothing; with --cheats ammo the bomb is kept, and the shopkeeper, Link's bombs full, sells none.

# The compact text (--text compact, Enhanced alone), English (US) laid out (the counters of ages/checks.tsv): shop.route's price and its choice, OK or No thanks, which keep their layout, and the bombs bought.

# The text box drawn by the host (--text-box-check, the figures of ages/checks.tsv): the intro's dialogues and cutscenes, its symbols, and shop.route's price and its choice, classic and compact; the run hashes those of the rows without the check.
# intro.route with the item hotkeys' slots: the hotbar never over the opening's framed pictures (Din's scene) nor in its cutscenes (5772 frames before).
# The wide text box (--text-box wide, the counters of ages/checks.tsv), classic and compact: shop.route's price and its choice, OK or No thanks, which keep their layout, at the box's left.
# Text size Very large (--text-size xlarge, the counters of ages/checks.tsv): the wide box twice as large in Far, compact: the shop's price and its choice.
# dungeon.route with the status bar laid out: a dungeon's keys in the money's block, sixteen hearts (the tightened layout), far and near 4:3.

# dungeon-diagonal.route: Link enters 4:57, a large room of a dungeon, by dungeon.route's inputs (his place jumps once as he enters it, as in dungeon.route), then walks six diagonals across it, written by hand. With the sub-pixel camera he is drawn at his exact place there, as outdoors, and on the ground he never steps across then down in turn on a diagonal, x and y crossing their pixels on frames of their own (enhanced.link_wobble, 65 times before): in the far view, where the room stands still, in the near one, where the band follows the game's window across and takes his fraction of a pixel with it, and in near 4:3, where it follows the window both ways. With the Pixel camera he walks the game's whole pixels, the zigzag held at 65.
# continuous-transitions.route with the status bar laid out: Subrosia's ore in the money's block (on SameBoy) and the white fades.
# overworld.route with the status bar laid out in the medium view.

# line-dungeon.route: seasons/dungeon.route's keys with the transitions at the line, through the dungeon's large rooms, where the line's comparisons leave the game's own bounds: no coordinate taken for one wrapped below zero (transitions.line_wraps), where x from 192 was put back on 0 and the transitions to the left chained into rooms off the dungeon's map; the same jumps as dungeon.route's. His sprite goes back on the screen against the step before twice across, as on dungeon.route, and 15 times down, as with the previous camera (enhanced.link_backsteps, _y).

# continuous-transitions.route with every feature at once that hooks the game, the transitions at the line, a language, the wide box, the compact and the instant text, the swim's hold, the cheats and the item hotkeys: every hook installed (39; the table held 32, and the line's four made the item hotkeys or the text box lose theirs).

column3: --continuous-line --language fr --text-box wide --text compact --text-speed instant --swim-hold --cheats no-damage,ammo,rupees --hotkeys-live use

column1: # line-lost-woods.route: turned back up during the scroll down from 0:30 into the Lost Woods (0:40), whose own transition leads every scroll but the one to the right back into 0:40: the walk back stops at the line (transitions.back_line_frames) and never goes past it into 0:30 (transitions.back_past_frames), no transition back forced from there (transitions.back_reversals); the game's own scroll up at the line then takes Link to 0:40, where he walked 5 px on 0:30's ground before and the forced scroll brought him into 0:40 all the same.

# line-corners.route: diagonals through two corners with the transitions at the line, written by hand from diagonal-crossings.route's keys: the corner of 0:d7, 0:d8, 0:e7 and 0:e8 up-left, the corner of 0:d6, 0:d7, 0:e6 and 0:e7 down-left and back up-right; every room the scrolls enter and every room beside has no object that may take the controls (0:d6, 0:d8, 0:f7 have some). Carried across during the first scroll, Link goes on at his pace past the line into the room beside, its collisions predicted from the ROM's tables (its tileset of the season, layout, substitutions and collisions), and the scroll into it starts from where he stands at the frame that ends the first (transitions.cross_started); each room beside predicted is what the game then loads (transitions.beside_matched). The ghost's failures are diagonal-crossings.route's own, before the corners. A savestate loaded in the last corner's second scroll gives the same steps (enhanced.reload_transition_differing), and no room shows black after it. As the scroll left out of 0:e7 starts (3610, 3611) he stands on the room's first column, his left column at x 0 in the OAM, drawn whole (enhanced.link_left_line_frames, a frame more since his sprite follows the game's own step at the frame that starts a scroll on foot), where it was left out.
